description:
Operator decision 2026-10-10 (asked during the Auto-mode run): only the control panel is reachable from the internet; Jellyfin, Radarr, Sonarr and Prowlarr stay home-only (reached at their LAN addresses, or over Tailscale when away).

Back up CT 120 (caddy-proxy, 192.168.1.127)'s /etc/caddy/Caddyfile, then make the site block `defrusciohomelab.duckdns.org` hold only the panel: `reverse_proxy 192.168.1.25:3001` (CT 111, whose own Basic auth stays the gate). Remove the /jellyfin, /prowlarr, /radarr and /sonarr routes. Validate, then reload Caddy. Do not touch the certificate or DNS.

Done when `pct exec 120 -- caddy validate --config /etc/caddy/Caddyfile --adapter caddyfile` answers `Valid configuration`, `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' --resolve defrusciohomelab.duckdns.org:443:192.168.1.127 https://defrusciohomelab.duckdns.org/` answers 401, and `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' --resolve defrusciohomelab.duckdns.org:443:192.168.1.127 https://defrusciohomelab.duckdns.org/radarr/` answers 401 (the panel's gate, no longer Radarr's 302).

Operator decision 2026-10-10: Tailscale should give access to the whole home network (every app at its 192.168.1.x address) when away. Tailscale runs directly on the Proxmox host (pve, 100.84.253.90).

On the host: turn on IPv4 forwarding persistently (a file under /etc/sysctl.d/, then apply it), and advertise the subnet with `tailscale set --advertise-routes=192.168.1.0/24` — `tailscale set` keeps the host's other Tailscale settings. Approving the advertised route in the Tailscale admin console (login.tailscale.com → Machines → pve → Edit route settings) is the operator's, in their own account.

Done when `sysctl -n net.ipv4.ip_forward` answers 1, and — after the operator has approved the route — `tailscale status --json | grep -c 192.168.1.0/24` answers at least 1.

Operator decision 2026-10-10: friends outside the house can join the Palworld server on VM 106 (palworld-server, MAC BC:24:11:E8:9F:7A, 192.168.1.44). ADD151 opens udp 8211 from anywhere in its firewall. The rest is the operator's, in the My Spectrum app (Services → Router → Advanced Settings → Port Forwarding & IP Reservations): reserve 192.168.1.44 for that MAC, then Add Port Assignment UDP 8211 → 192.168.1.44:8211. Friends connect to defrusciohomelab.duckdns.org:8211.

Done when the operator reports both saved, and `grep 'dport 8211' /etc/pve/firewall/106.fw` on the host shows `IN ACCEPT -p udp -dport 8211` with no source restriction (ADD151 put the open rule in VM 106's own file, before its GROUP game line).

🔁 Updated after the measured address of VM 106 (palworld-server): `192.168.1.106` → `192.168.1.44` (ip).

prompt_template: Operator decision: Whole-GPU passthrough to dedicated AI VM (suggested) vs Docker GPU passthrough inside VM vs LXC GPU passthrough. Tradeoffs: whole-GPU locks GPU to one VM but most stable/documented for P40; Docker adds complexity with driver/hang issues; LXC has weaker isolation and less P40 documentation. Suggested: whole-GPU passthrough.
